exact_original_task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n>=2, h a smooth positive Hermitian form and dV a smooth strictly positive probability. Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. PSH(X,h) consists of genuine canonical quasi-plurisubharmonic functions u with h+dd^c u>=0; no null-set alteration of subharmonic values is allowed. MA_h^ext(u) is the extended non-pluripolar measure obtained by truncation on finite levels, possibly of infinite total mass.
For nonzero f>=0 in L1(dV), let b_h(f) be the maximal c>=0 for which some genuine h-psh u satisfies MA_h^ext(u)>=c f dV; equivalently it is the decreasing limit of the continuous-equation normalization scalars for min(f,k). Assume b=b_h(f)>0. Let S_f be the normalized threshold subsolutions, and Phi_f their greatest genuine member with sup_X Phi_f=0, as in the known threshold theorem.
A smooth Gauduchon test current T is a smooth positive (n-1,n-1) form satisfying dd^c T=0 and integral_X h wedge T=1. If T=gamma^(n-1), define k_T=(gamma^n/dV)^((n-1)/n), extending continuously to smooth semipositive forms. Put p=f^(1/n) and D_p(T)=integral_X p k_T dV. The known dual threshold formula is sup_T D_p(T)=b^(-1/n). Suppose it is attained by a smooth semipositive T, strictly positive outside a proper analytic set Z.
For 0<delta<1, define the smaller-background obstacle envelope P_(delta h)(Phi_f)=(sup{v in PSH(X,delta h):v<=Phi_f})^*, with upper semicontinuous regularization. Calling this envelope genuine requires a nonempty competitor family and a canonical delta-h-psh envelope not identically -infinity. This is an obstacle envelope, not a singularity-type zero-obstacle envelope.
Original S16: find additional intrinsic or geometric hypotheses making this smaller-background envelope genuine for some delta<1, and determine regularity across Z. More generally decide whether moment or entropy control forces that envelope condition, or identify a rigorously proved failure. For a smooth positive maximizing sequence T_j, set d_j=D_p(T_j) tending to b^(-1/n) and nu_j=d_j^(-1)p k_(T_j)dV. Uniform first moments mean integral_X(-v)dnu_j<=C for every j and every h-psh v with sup v=0. Uniform entropy means nu_j=a_j dV and integral_X a_j log(a_j)dV<=C. These conditions supply a fixed lower barrier, scalar estimates and selected-sequence uniform integrability, but the known proof does not supply the smaller-background envelope.
Known background: a smooth semipositive maximizer positive off Z already gives an exact finite-mass global threshold equation, smoothness off Z, uniqueness of threshold subsolutions up to constants and normalized whole-family L1 convergence as the exponential parameter goes to zero. Genuineness of the smaller-background envelope upgrades convergence to capacity. Bounded Phi_f makes that envelope genuine by a constant competitor. If f is Lp for p>1, the solution is continuous and convergence uniform. These known bounded/Lp cases and off-Z smoothness alone are not new answers to S16. No candidate family, conclusion or proof is supplied.

immutable_clarified_full_review.report:
The argument meets the restricted sufficient-condition alternative in the completion criteria. Condition (G) proves genuineness of every smaller-background obstacle envelope without assuming boundedness or Lp data. The sublinear singularity condition gives a separate explicit competitor construction. The extension theorem proves smoothness across Z under its additional smooth-root, rank and zero-Lelong hypotheses. These conclusions do not settle general S16 or either moment/entropy implication.

I independently checked n1–n3 and retrieved the primary sources listed below. The unavailable Demailly locator was replaced by another university-hosted copy of the same authored manuscript. The cited product, contact, envelope, uniqueness, Gauduchon, Lelong, stratification and support results have the required hypotheses. Task-granted threshold facts are used within their stated scope and are excluded from the external-premise list. The reported symbolic checks and artifacts are unnecessary for mathematical acceptance.

For n1, put V=∫h^n. Bedford–Taylor recursion gives (dd^c w)^ℓ=dd^c(w(dd^c w)^(ℓ−1)) for bounded quasi-psh w, interpreted through local smooth-factor expansions. Distributional integration by parts against h^(n−ℓ) therefore kills every nonconstant term under (G); the ℓ=n term is killed by dd^c1=0. Thus bounded h-psh functions have mass V. Truncation and locality give MA_h^ext(w)(X)≤V for arbitrary genuine h-psh w. Integrating the bounded normalization equations and using the task-granted limiting characterization yields b=V/∫f dV. Every threshold subsolution consequently has full mass and satisfies MA_h^ext(u)=bf dV. No maximizer is needed for these deductions.

The competitor construction is valid. For a>1, u_j=max(u,−j) and w_j=P_h(a u_j) are bounded, with −aj≤w_j≤0. The source defines envelopes using quasi-everywhere constraints. Here obstacle and competitor become psh after adding one common local smooth majorizer; their almost-everywhere order passes through convolution to their canonical pointwise representatives. Thus the source envelope is the required pointwise envelope. Contact support and comparison in the background ah—not in h—give MA_h(w_j)≤a^n 1_{w_j=a u_j}MA_h(u_j). For j≥M, locality and full mass give exactly MA_h(u_j)({u_j≤−M})=V−MA_h^ext(u)({u>−M})=MA_h^ext(u)({u≤−M}). This tail tends to zero, including at poles, because the measure is finite and non-pluripolar. Choosing M with a^n times that tail less than V forces sup w_j≥−aM. The decreasing sequence cannot converge identically to −∞: compactness applied to the nested open sets {w_j<−aM−1} would contradict this bound. Its genuine limit w satisfies w≤au pointwise. Hence v_δ=δw, with δ=1/a, is an actual δh-psh competitor below u. The regularized supremum remains below the upper semicontinuous obstacle; finite maxima and distributional closure preserve the δh Hessian bound. This establishes the envelope's actual genuineness.

The zero-Lelong deduction is also justified. A strictly positive normalized Gauduchon form G gives ∫(δh+dd^c v_δ)∧G=δ even for unbounded genuine potentials. On each fixed coordinate ball, adding δKω_0 produces a positive closed current whose trace mass is O(δ). The fixed-radius Lelong estimate, a finite atlas and order comparison yield ν(u,x)≤C_hδ uniformly in x. Letting δ decrease to zero proves vanishing everywhere. The degenerate maximizing test is not substituted for this strictly positive auxiliary form.

For n3, condition (7) is an explicit additional quantitative hypothesis, not an assumed envelope conclusion. With α<β<1 and εβC≤δ, K=B+sup_{t≥1}(At^α−εt^β) is finite. The increasing convex function χ(t)=−ε(1−t)^β has 0<χ′≤εβ and χ″≥0. Truncating ψ, smoothing locally and passing to decreasing limits proves dd^cχ(ψ)≥−εβCh. Thus v_δ=χ(ψ)−K is genuine, not identically −∞, and pointwise below Φ_f, including all poles. The divisor instance follows from Poincaré–Lelong with precisely the task's normalization. Competitors for every δ again imply zero Lelong numbers. No moment or entropy estimate is used to establish condition (7).

For n2, integrated matrix AM–GM is applied only where γ is positive and Φ_f is smooth. The threshold equation and attainment make the lower bound integrate to 1, while the positive current A=h+dd^cΦ_f has total T-trace 1. Consequently the gap vanishes and A=rγ on X\Z, including the r=0 case. The rank-at-least-two condition makes ξ↦ξ∧γ injective: each coordinate of ξ can be detected using a positive coordinate two-plane disjoint from it. Its smooth left inverse exists globally by compactness. Differentiation therefore gives dr=α−rβ with globally smooth coefficients, and |d log(1+r)|≤C. Analytic strata have real codimension at least two, so bad endpoints of segments form null cones. A generic intermediate point gives short two-segment paths avoiding Z; a finite connected chart cover gives bounded global connecting lengths. These facts bound r and then dr, yielding a Lipschitz extension. Since Z has zero volume, the first-order equation holds weakly across Z and bootstraps the extension to smoothness.

The residual R=A−rγ is precisely A's positive measure part carried by Z, hence is positive. Crucially, d(rγ)=dh makes R closed before the support theorem is applied. The theorem reduces it to divisorial currents, and zero Lelong numbers eliminate their coefficients. Thus dd^cΦ_f is smooth globally. Taking a Euclidean trace gives a Poisson equation with smooth right side, so local elliptic regularity makes Φ_f smooth; canonical representatives ensure equality everywhere. This establishes regularity across Z under the extra hypotheses. It asserts no smoothness of obstacle envelopes at their free boundaries.

Both attained examples check out. On the Hopf surface, scaling invariance makes h=s^(−1)dd^c s descend, and the dimension-two radial trace sF″+2F′=0 for F=1/s proves dd^c h=0. The quotient is compact and connected. Its non-Kähler assertion can also be verified directly using the nonzero, semipositive, exact descended form dd^c log s and Stokes against a hypothetical Kähler metric. Small smooth perturbations A=h+dd^c(εq) remain positive. Mass invariance gives b=1, T=A/V has the required normalization, and AM–GM gives D_p(S)≤∫A∧S=1 for every normalized positive test, with equality for T. On the quadric, the defining gradient never vanishes, the projection is a double cover, and its differential has ranks n and n−1 off and on the ramification divisor. The displayed logarithmic potential gives A=h+dd^c u with −log2≤u≤0. Change of variables for the double cover gives ∫A^n=2; Kähler Stokes gives V=2. The stated T and γ then have exactly the claimed normalization, attainment and rank properties. These smooth examples verify compatibility of the hypotheses; they are not presented as unbounded counterexamples.

The projective example is likewise correctly scoped. Its radial eigenvalues give (dd^cF)^n the radial density d(q(s)^n), with the task's normalization. Since q(0)=0, annular Stokes and the truncations' unchanged boundary flux prove full non-pluripolar mass 1. The density asymptotic s^(−n)(1−log s)^(n(α−1)−1) has an integrable L1 tail and a divergent Lp tail for every p>1. Mass invariance establishes b=1, and full-mass Kähler uniqueness identifies the normalized threshold potential. The source convention is accommodated by halving the potentials, preserving all currents and measures. If a specified smooth maximizer existed, AM–GM equality would give T=tA^(n−1) off the pole. Smoothness extends this identity across any additional degeneracy locus there. Closedness of A yields dd^c t∧A^(n−1)=0. Every eigenvalue of A tends to infinity at the pole, so bounded smooth T forces t→0. A positive interior maximum then contradicts the strong maximum principle on the connected punctured manifold. Thus the example provably lacks the required maximizer and is not an S16 failure example.

On a compact complex manifold, for smooth positive Hermitian ω and a bounded quasicontinuous obstacle g, the upper-regularized envelope with quasi-everywhere constraints is bounded ω-psh, lies below g quasi-everywhere, and its Monge–Ampère measure is carried by {P_ω(g)=g}. [Guedj–Lu, Definition 2.2 and Theorem 2.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2106.04272).

A locally uniformly upper-bounded psh family has a psh upper-regularized supremum. Decreasing psh limits are psh or identically −∞ on each connected component; nontrivial limits are locally integrable. [Demailly, I.4.17 and I.5.4–5.7](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf).

Every connected compact complex n-manifold, n≥2, admits a smooth strictly positive Hermitian γ with dd^cγ^(n−1)=0. Its power can be scaled to satisfy ∫Xh∧γ^(n−1)=1 for any specified smooth positive h. [Gauduchon, Theorem 2](https://www.numdam.org/article/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf).

For positive closed (1,1)-currents B on B(x,R)⊂C^n, ν(B,x)≤C_nR^(−2n+2) times their trace mass. Genuine quasi-psh v≤u satisfy ν(u,x)≤ν(v,x). [Demailly, III.5.7–5.8 and III.6.9](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf).

Proper analytic subsets of complex n-manifolds admit locally finite stratifications by smooth complex manifolds of dimension at most n−1. [Demailly, II.5.6](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf).

Positive closed (1,1)-currents supported on proper analytic subsets are locally finite sums ∑c_i[D_i] over divisorial components, with constant c_i≥0; no nonzero such current is supported in complex codimension at least two. [Demailly, III.2.10–2.14](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf).

For a nonzero holomorphic section s of a Hermitian line bundle (L,H), dd^c log|s|_H²=[div(s)]−Θ_H under dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π), where Θ_H=−dd^c log|e|_H² for a local nonvanishing holomorphic frame e. [Demailly, III.2.15 and V.13.2](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf).

For a smooth real second-order elliptic operator with locally positive definite principal symbol and no zeroth-order term on a connected manifold, a C² solution of Lt=0 attaining its global maximum at an interior point is constant. [Gauduchon, Section 2, maximum-principle proposition](https://www.numdam.org/article/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf).

Independent reconstruction A.

Conventions and foundations. Throughout dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π), and d^c=i(bar∂−∂)/(4π). Functions have their canonical quasi-psh representatives. The imported foundations are precisely the supplied bounded Hermitian Bedford–Taylor calculus, Guedj–Lu contact comparison and bounded-obstacle envelope theorem, the granted threshold/scalar characterization, and the explicitly permitted elementary local psh and Lelong facts. The specified h is never conformally replaced.

Canonical inequalities and admissible obstacles. A canonical quasi-psh function g satisfies
  g(x)=lim_{r↓0} average_{B(x,r)} g,
including when g(x)=−∞. Indeed, add a smooth local function to make g psh, use the psh mean-value limit, and subtract the smooth mean. Thus an almost-everywhere inequality between canonical quasi-psh functions holds at every point. In particular, the quasi-everywhere inequalities furnished by the envelope theorem become pointwise inequalities for the obstacles used below.

Bounded quasi-psh obstacles are quasi-continuous and hence quasi-lower-semicontinuous. Here is the local derivation needed for this application. Reduce to a bounded psh function w and bounded smooth psh regularizations w_l↓w on a smaller coordinate chart. Put s_l=w_l−w≥0 and Q_l=w_l+w. With nested compactly supported cutoffs, for 0≤v≤1 psh consider
  I_{k,m}=∫χ s_l(dd^c Q_l)^k(dd^c v)^m ω_0^(n−k−m),  k+m≤n.
For m≥1, integration by parts and Cauchy–Schwarz give, with a larger cutoff on the right,
  I_{k,m}≤C(I_{k+1,m−1}+I_{k,m−1})^(1/2).
To check this, write χ=θ² and integrate one dd^c v factor. The ds_l term is controlled by the square root of its gradient energy times the gradient energy of v. The cutoff term is controlled by C I_{k,m−1}^{1/2}, because s_l²≤C s_l. For the remaining closed positive mixed product S, integration by parts and absorption give
  ∫χ ds_l∧d^c s_l∧S
  ≤2∫χ s_l dd^c Q_l∧S+C∫χ′ s_l ω_0∧S.
Here −s_l dd^c s_l≤s_l dd^c Q_l. The gradient energy of v is uniformly bounded by applying dd^c(v²)=2v dd^c v+2dv∧d^c v and cutoff Stokes. Repeated cutoff Stokes bounds all mixed masses by the uniform bounds of the potentials. Perform the calculation first for smooth approximations and pass to bounded decreasing limits using the assessed BT calculus. For m=0, I_{k,0}→0: the weighted products with weights w_l and w have the same limit by bounded decreasing BT continuity in its recursive weighted form. Iteration therefore gives
  sup_{0≤v≤1}∫_K s_l(dd^c v)^n→0.
Consequently Cap_K{w_l−w>η}→0 for every η>0. Choose a subsequence with summable exceptional capacities and errors 2^(−l). These exceptional sets are open because w is upper semicontinuous and w_l is continuous. Outside their union the subsequence converges uniformly, proving local quasi-continuity. Adding smooth functions and using a finite chart cover gives the Hermitian assertion. The capacity comparison is elementary: choose smooth ρ with dd^cρ≥ω on a chart; a normalized ω-psh test plus ρ is a uniformly bounded local psh test, and its local top product dominates the Hermitian top product. Rescaling compares the capacities. This applies equally to δh.

Uniform Lelong bound. There is a constant L_h bounding the Lelong number of every genuine h-psh function at every point, independently of additive constants. Choose a supplied smooth strictly positive normalized Gauduchon test T_0. For H_w=h+dd^c w≥0, distributional Stokes gives ∫H_w∧T_0=1. Strict positivity on compact X uniformly bounds the trace mass of H_w. On each fixed smaller coordinate ball choose smooth ρ with dd^cρ≥h. The closed positive current dd^c(w+ρ)=H_w+(dd^cρ−h) then has uniformly bounded trace mass. The permitted local Lelong mass estimate and a finite cover give ν(w,x)≤L_h. Therefore, if for every δ>0 an actual δh-psh function v_δ≤u exists, Lelong comparison gives
  0≤ν(u,x)≤ν(v_δ,x)=δν(v_δ/δ,x)≤δL_h.
Letting δ↓0 proves ν(u,x)=0.

Mass conservation. Assume dd^c(h^k)=0 for 1≤k<n, and V=∫h^n. For every bounded genuine h-psh w, expansion and weighted Stokes give
  ∫(h+dd^c w)^n=V.
Indeed, for 1≤j≤n,
  ∫(dd^c w)^j∧h^(n−j)
  =∫w(dd^c w)^(j−1)∧dd^c(h^(n−j))=0;
for j=n use dd^c1=0. The signed mixed terms are defined by the supplied smooth-factor BT expansion; bounded approximation and weighted Stokes justify the computation for nonsmooth bounded w. The identical argument for δh gives total mass δ^n V.

For any genuine h-psh u, shift its supremum to zero and set u_j=max(u,−j), μ_j=(h+dd^c u_j)^n, μ=MA_h^ext(u). Finite-level locality identifies μ_j with μ on {u>−j}. Since μ_j(X)=V and these sets exhaust the non-pluripolar measure, μ(X)≤V. In particular the extended mass is finite on this background.

Let M=∫f dV>0. Any subsolution μ≥c f dV gives c≤V/M. Conversely the granted bounded-equation normalization characterization for f_k=min(f,k), together with bounded mass conservation, gives b_k∫f_k dV=V. Passing to the stipulated decreasing limit yields b_h(f)=V/M. For a threshold subsolution μ≥b_h(f)f dV, the right side has mass V while μ(X)≤V. Hence μ(X)=V and μ=b_h(f)f dV.

Actual canonical smaller-background competitor. Let μ(X)=V and fix 0<δ<1. Put v_j=P_(δh)(u_j). The constant −j is a competitor, so the assessed bounded-envelope theorem applies; −j≤v_j≤0. Its quasi-everywhere inequality v_j≤u_j is everywhere by the canonical mean-value argument. Let C_j={v_j=u_j}. Contact support, positivity after adding (1−δ)h, and the assessed h-contact comparison yield
  δ^n V=∫_{C_j}MA_(δh)(v_j)
  ≤∫_{C_j}MA_h(v_j)≤μ_j(C_j).
Both v_j and u_j are bounded h-psh, as required for that comparison.

Choose K>0 such that μ({u>−K})>(1−δ^n)V. For j>K, locality gives
  μ_j({u_j≤−K})=V−μ({u>−K})<δ^n V.
If sup v_j<−K, then C_j⊂{u_j≤−K}, contradicting the preceding inequality. Thus sup v_j≥−K. The envelopes decrease with their obstacles. Their decreasing limit v_δ is canonical δh-psh or identically −∞. To exclude the latter, take maximizers x_j and a convergent subsequence x_j→x. For each fixed l and all sufficiently large j, v_l(x_j)≥v_j(x_j)≥−K. Upper semicontinuity implies v_l(x)≥−K, hence v_δ(x)≥−K.

At every point,
  v_δ=lim_j v_j≤lim_j u_j=u.
This includes every pole: v_δ=−∞ wherever u=−∞. Thus v_δ is an actual canonical global competitor. Every other δh-psh competitor w≤u satisfies w≤v_j for every j and hence w≤v_δ. Since v_δ itself is a competitor, the raw supremum equals v_δ, already canonically upper semicontinuous. Consequently P_(δh)(u)=v_δ is genuine for every 0<δ<1. The uniform Lelong argument proves zero Lelong numbers. No dual attainment was used.

The non-Kähler Hopf instance. On C²\{0}, let s=|z|², Ω=dd^c s, h=s^(−1)Ω. The free properly discontinuous holomorphic action z↦2z multiplies s and Ω by four, so h descends smoothly and positively to the connected compact complex surface; a closed radial annulus is a compact fundamental region. The chain rule gives
  dd^c h=(−s^(−2)Ω+2s^(−3)ds∧d^c s)∧Ω=0,
because ds∧d^c s∧Ω=(s/2)Ω² in dimension two. However dh=−s^(−2)ds∧Ω is nonzero; at (r,0), its radial-first-coordinate and two-real-second-coordinate component is nonzero. Thus this specified h is not closed. With the stipulated normalization, the angularly integrated radial measure Ω² is 2s ds. On 1≤s≤4 the quotient volume is
  V=∫_1^4 2 ds/s=4 log 2.

For nonconstant smooth real q, choose sufficiently small nonzero ε so A=h+dd^c(εq)>0, and set u=εq−sup(εq), dV=h²/V, f=A²/dV, T=A/V. Mass conservation gives ∫A²=V, so M=V and b_h(f)=1. The normalized smooth u solves MA_h(u)=f dV. Moreover dd^c T=0 and ∫h∧T=V^(−1)∫h∧A=1 by dd^c h=0 and Stokes. T is smooth strictly positive, with root γ=A/V, and direct substitution gives D_p(T)=∫A²/V=1.

For every other normalized smooth positive Gauduchon test S=η^(n−1), arithmetic–geometric mean gives
  (A^n)^(1/n)(η^n)^((n−1)/n)≤A∧η^(n−1).
In an η-unitary frame, the right side is the arithmetic mean of the eigenvalues times η^n and the left side their geometric mean times η^n. Every strictly positive (n−1,n−1) test has a smooth positive root: in the normalized cofactor identification, a test matrix B>0 has root matrix (det B)^(1/(n−1))B^(−1), whose adjugate is B. Uniqueness makes this construction coordinate invariant. Here n=2. Therefore
  D_p(S)≤∫A∧S=∫h∧S+∫u dd^c S=1.
T is an actual maximizer over ALL normalized positive smooth tests. Granted attained uniqueness identifies Phi_f=u canonically.

notes.text:
Independent reconstruction B.

Write U=X\Z and A=h+dd^c Phi_f. The exact attained equation, finite mass and smoothness on U are granted background. Assume T=γ^(n−1), where γ is globally smooth semipositive with complex rank at least two everywhere, and Phi_f has zero Lelong numbers. On U, positivity of T implies positive definiteness of γ; A is smooth nonnegative there.

Proportionality from dual equality. The global measure β=A∧T is positive and well-defined because T is smooth semipositive and A is a positive order-zero current. Distributional Gauduchon Stokes gives β(X)=∫h∧T=1. On U, the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality established in n1 gives
  β≥(A^n)^(1/n)(γ^n)^((n−1)/n)=b^(1/n)p k_T dV.
The right side has mass b^(1/n)D_p(T)=1 and gives no mass to the proper analytic set Z. Equality of total masses forces equality on U and β(Z)=0. Equality in arithmetic–geometric mean for nonnegative eigenvalues says precisely that
  A=λγ on U,
where λ≥0 is smooth. This includes λ=0; no positivity of A or lower bound on f is assumed.

The rank condition. On real one-forms define L_γ(ξ)=ξ∧γ. It is injective when rank_C γ≥2. Diagonalize γ on its active real subspace W, of dimension 2r≥4. A complementary component of ξ cannot cancel an active component because the complementary degrees differ. On W, ξ∧γ=0 implies ξ∧γ^(r−1)=0 by wedging with γ^(r−2). The latter map from one-forms to (2r−1)-forms is an isomorphism in a symplectic basis. Hence ξ=0. With smooth background inner products,
  J=(L_γ*L_γ)^(−1)L_γ*
is a globally smooth left inverse, including at rank changes.

Since dA=dh, on U the proportionality gives
  dλ=a+λc,
  a=J(dh), c=−J(dγ),
where a and c are globally smooth one-forms. We prove extension of λ rather than assuming it.

Short paths and scalar extension. In a small real coordinate ball B, a and c are bounded. Two points of B/2\Z can be joined inside B by two line segments avoiding Z with total length at most four times the radius. Indeed, for a fixed endpoint, bad intermediate points belong to the cone of real rays through Z. A proper complex analytic set has real dimension at most 2n−2, so each such cone has dimension at most 2n−1 and Lebesgue measure zero. This can be checked on the countably many smooth strata of the analytic set and bounded intervals of the ray parameter. Thus an admissible intermediate point exists in any open ball. For endpoints distance d apart, an intermediate point in a radius-d ball gives length at most 3d within a slightly larger ball.

Fix x_0∈B/2\Z. Along these paths,
  |dλ/ds|≤K(1+λ).
Gronwall uniformly bounds λ by its finite value at x_0 and the bounded path length. The equation then uniformly bounds its gradient. The length-3d paths make λ locally Lipschitz on B/4\Z. It extends uniquely and nonnegatively across Z; the local extensions agree. Since Z has Lebesgue measure zero, the extended weak derivative still satisfies dλ=a+λc almost everywhere. The right side is continuous, so λ is C¹. Repeated differentiation bootstraps λ to C∞ globally.

Positive residual and analytic support. Set R=A−λγ. It has order zero and is supported on Z. The smooth form λγ has no mass on Z. Decomposing the matrix-valued measure A into restrictions to U and Z, its U-restriction is λγ and its Z-restriction is positive. Consequently R is precisely A restricted to Z and is positive. This proves the positivity of the residual rather than assuming positivity of a difference. Furthermore
  dR=dh−d(λγ)
is smooth and vanishes on dense U, hence vanishes everywhere.

At regular points of every irreducible divisorial component D of Z, the assessed support theorem for closed order-zero currents gives R=c_D[D], with c_D≥0 constant on the connected regular part. Let Q=Σc_D[D], a finite sum. Outside an analytic subset Y of complex dimension at most n−2, R=Q. Divisor integration currents give no mass to Y: their regular parts give no volume to smaller-dimensional analytic subsets, and their singular loci carry no integration-current mass. Thus R−Q=R restricted to Y is positive, closed and order zero. It is a normal current of bidimension (n−1,n−1) supported in dimension less than n−1. The supplied Demailly support theorem makes it zero. Therefore R=Σc_D[D]. At a generic regular point of D its Lelong number is c_D. Smooth forms have zero Lelong numbers, and the zero Lelong numbers of Phi_f make those of A and R zero. Every c_D is zero.

It follows that A=λγ is globally smooth and dd^c Phi_f=λγ−h is smooth. Taking the Euclidean trace locally and using distributional elliptic regularity makes Phi_f a smooth distributional potential. The canonical mean-value argument in n1 identifies this smooth representative with Phi_f at every point. This proves smoothness across all of Z. It requires the stated globally smooth root, not merely a continuous root, and claims no smoothness of an obstacle envelope at a free boundary.

The genuinely degenerating quadric. For n≥3 let
  X={ [w:z_0:…:z_n]∈P^(n+1): w²=Σz_i² },
  F([w:z])=[z], Z={w=0}⊂X.
The gradient (2w,−2z_0,…,−2z_n) never vanishes at a projective point, so X is smooth of dimension n and compact. Its quadratic form has rank n+2>2 and cannot factor into linear forms; hence X is irreducible and connected. F is globally defined because z=0 would force w=0. In a chart z_j≠0, its equation is monic quadratic in w/z_j. Thus F is a two-sheeted cover off the smooth branch quadric Σz_i²=0 and a branched double cover globally. Z is a nonempty smooth proper divisor.

When w≠0, dF is invertible. When w=0, its kernel is exactly the one-dimensional w-direction: fixing all z-ratios leaves the tangent condition 2wδw=0, while the z-variations satisfy one independent quadric relation. Therefore rank_C dF=n off Z and n−1 on Z.

Use normalized Fubini–Study forms, locally dd^c log Σ|coordinates|², with ∫_(P^n)ω_FS^n=1. Define
  h=ω_FS|_X, A=F*ω_FS,
  u=log(Σ|z_i|²/(|w|²+Σ|z_i|²)).
The numerator is nowhere zero on X, so u is globally smooth. Local potentials give A=h+dd^c u. Since |w|²=|Σz_i²|≤Σ|z_i|²,
  −log 2≤u≤0.
On Z, u=0, so sup u=0. A is smooth semipositive and has ranks n and n−1 as claimed.

The double cover gives ∫_X A^n=2, since smooth top forms give no mass to the branch set. Closedness and Stokes give
  V=∫h^n=∫h∧A^(n−1)=2.
Set
  dV=h^n/2, f=A^n/dV,
  T=A^(n−1)/2, γ=A/2^(1/(n−1)).
The density f is smooth nonnegative, positive off Z, and ∫f dV=2. The Kähler background satisfies A's condition in n1; hence b=V/M=1. The normalized u solves the exact equation. T is smooth semipositive, positive off Z, dd^c T=0 and ∫h∧T=1. Its globally smooth root γ has rank at least n−1≥2 everywhere. Direct substitution yields D_p(T)=∫A^n/2=1.

For every normalized positive smooth Gauduchon test S, n1's AM–GM and Stokes calculation yields D_p(S)≤∫A∧S=1. Thus T is an actual maximizer over the whole test class. It is also approximated by positive normalized Gauduchon tests
  (T+εh^(n−1))/(1+2ε),
whose D_p tends to one by continuity of the determinant density. Granted attained uniqueness identifies Phi_f=u. This verifies all geometry and exact constants. The example genuinely degenerates along Z but remains smooth and bounded. In dimension two rank at least two would instead exclude degeneration.

notes.text:
Independent reconstruction C.

Explicit canonical competitors on the specified arbitrary h. Assume ψ is genuine global quasi-psh, ψ≤0, dd^cψ≥−Ch, C>0, and canonically pointwise
  Phi_f≥−A(1−ψ)^α−B,
where A>0 and 0<α<1, with the stated −∞ interpretation at poles. Given 0<δ<1, choose t≥1 sufficiently large that
  CAαt^(α−1)≤δ,
and define
  v_δ=−A(t−ψ)^α−B,
with value −∞ at every pole of ψ. The function χ_t(s)=−A(t−s)^α−B is increasing and convex for s≤0, with 0<χ_t′≤Aαt^(α−1) and χ_t″≥0. Hence
  dd^cχ_t(ψ)≥−CAαt^(α−1)h≥−δh.
For singular ψ, this chain rule is justified by ψ_j=max(ψ,−j), local smooth psh regularizations after adding a fixed smooth local potential, the smooth chain rule, and bounded decreasing limits. Smoothness of h makes the error in the lower Hessian bound tend to zero. The positive second-derivative term is retained. Thus χ_t(ψ_j) are bounded δh-psh and decrease to χ_t(ψ). The limit is not identically −∞ because ψ is genuine and finite almost everywhere, and it is canonical, including its pole values.

Since t≥1,
  v_δ≤−A(1−ψ)^α−B≤Phi_f
at every point. This is an actual global competitor. The upper-regularized supremum of the nonempty competitor family is genuine δh-psh. To justify this canonically, the family is locally uniformly bounded above by the upper semicontinuous Phi_f and bounded below by v_δ. On sufficiently small coordinate balls, add quadratic potentials with constant Hessians dominating δh with arbitrarily small errors; the upper envelope then becomes psh. Let the errors tend to zero to obtain dd^c P≥−δh. The lower competitor excludes identically −∞. Upper regularization remains below Phi_f because Phi_f is upper semicontinuous; thus all required pole values are retained. Equivalently, the decreasing bounded envelopes P_(δh)(max(Phi_f,−j)) are bounded below by v_δ, and their limit is the same envelope by n1's maximality argument.

The all-δ competitors and n1's uniform Lelong bound prove ν(Phi_f,x)=0 everywhere. Together with exactly n2's globally smooth root and rank assumptions, this proves smooth extension across Z. Without those assumptions, this argument asserts neither boundedness nor continuity across Z.

Divisor logarithms. For an effective divisor D with defining section s of a line bundle L and smooth Hermitian metric H, set ψ=log|s|_H² minus its finite supremum. Poincaré–Lelong in the stipulated normalization gives
  dd^cψ=[D]−Θ_H.
Compactness gives Θ_H≤Ch for some C>0. Thus ψ is a permissible genuine global quasi-psh control function, canonically −∞ on D. This constructs ψ; it does not assert that an arbitrary Phi_f satisfies the required lower bound.

The projective example. On P^n, n≥2, let h=ω_FS, ∫h^n=1, dV=h^n, and
  ψ=log(Σ_(i=1)^n|z_i|²/Σ_(i=0)^n|z_i|²),
  u=1−(1−ψ)^α, 0<α<1,
  o=[1:0:…:0].
Local numerator potentials log Σ_(i=1)^n|z_i|² are psh with their canonical pole at o. Subtracting the local FS potential gives dd^cψ≥−h. Its sole pole is o; it is smooth elsewhere, ψ≤0, and ψ=0 along z_0=0.

For χ(s)=1−(1−s)^α,
  χ′(s)=α(1−s)^(α−1)≤α<1,
  χ″(s)=α(1−α)(1−s)^(α−2)>0.
The preceding composition argument gives genuine canonical h-psh u, smooth off o, u(o)=−∞, and sup u=0. In fact, globally as currents,
  h+dd^c u≥(1−α)h.
Off o this is immediate from
  h+dd^c u=(1−χ′)h+χ′(h+dd^cψ)+χ″dψ∧d^cψ;
truncation proves the global assertion. The quantitative bound is exact: A=1, B=−1, C=1. Actual smaller-background competitors are 1−(t−ψ)^α with t≥1 and αt^(α−1)≤δ. These also prove zero Lelong numbers. Full mass is established separately below.

notes.text:
Independent reconstruction A.

Conventions and foundations. Throughout dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π), and d^c=i(bar∂−∂)/(4π). Functions have their canonical quasi-psh representatives. The imported foundations are precisely the supplied bounded Hermitian Bedford–Taylor calculus, Guedj–Lu contact comparison and bounded-obstacle envelope theorem, the granted threshold/scalar characterization, and the explicitly permitted elementary local psh and Lelong facts. The specified h is never conformally replaced.

Canonical inequalities and admissible obstacles. A canonical quasi-psh function g satisfies
  g(x)=lim_{r↓0} average_{B(x,r)} g,
including when g(x)=−∞. Indeed, add a smooth local function to make g psh, use the psh mean-value limit, and subtract the smooth mean. Thus an almost-everywhere inequality between canonical quasi-psh functions holds at every point. In particular, the quasi-everywhere inequalities furnished by the envelope theorem become pointwise inequalities for the obstacles used below.

Bounded quasi-psh obstacles are quasi-continuous and hence quasi-lower-semicontinuous. Here is the local derivation needed for this application. Reduce to a bounded psh function w and bounded smooth psh regularizations w_l↓w on a smaller coordinate chart. Put s_l=w_l−w≥0 and Q_l=w_l+w. With nested compactly supported cutoffs, for 0≤v≤1 psh consider
  I_{k,m}=∫χ s_l(dd^c Q_l)^k(dd^c v)^m ω_0^(n−k−m),  k+m≤n.
For m≥1, integration by parts and Cauchy–Schwarz give, with a larger cutoff on the right,
  I_{k,m}≤C(I_{k+1,m−1}+I_{k,m−1})^(1/2).
To check this, write χ=θ² and integrate one dd^c v factor. The ds_l term is controlled by the square root of its gradient energy times the gradient energy of v. The cutoff term is controlled by C I_{k,m−1}^{1/2}, because s_l²≤C s_l. For the remaining closed positive mixed product S, integration by parts and absorption give
  ∫χ ds_l∧d^c s_l∧S
  ≤2∫χ s_l dd^c Q_l∧S+C∫χ′ s_l ω_0∧S.
Here −s_l dd^c s_l≤s_l dd^c Q_l. The gradient energy of v is uniformly bounded by applying dd^c(v²)=2v dd^c v+2dv∧d^c v and cutoff Stokes. Repeated cutoff Stokes bounds all mixed masses by the uniform bounds of the potentials. Perform the calculation first for smooth approximations and pass to bounded decreasing limits using the assessed BT calculus. For m=0, I_{k,0}→0: the weighted products with weights w_l and w have the same limit by bounded decreasing BT continuity in its recursive weighted form. Iteration therefore gives
  sup_{0≤v≤1}∫_K s_l(dd^c v)^n→0.
Consequently Cap_K{w_l−w>η}→0 for every η>0. Choose a subsequence with summable exceptional capacities and errors 2^(−l). These exceptional sets are open because w is upper semicontinuous and w_l is continuous. Outside their union the subsequence converges uniformly, proving local quasi-continuity. Adding smooth functions and using a finite chart cover gives the Hermitian assertion. The capacity comparison is elementary: choose smooth ρ with dd^cρ≥ω on a chart; a normalized ω-psh test plus ρ is a uniformly bounded local psh test, and its local top product dominates the Hermitian top product. Rescaling compares the capacities. This applies equally to δh.

Uniform Lelong bound. There is a constant L_h bounding the Lelong number of every genuine h-psh function at every point, independently of additive constants. Choose a supplied smooth strictly positive normalized Gauduchon test T_0. For H_w=h+dd^c w≥0, distributional Stokes gives ∫H_w∧T_0=1. Strict positivity on compact X uniformly bounds the trace mass of H_w. On each fixed smaller coordinate ball choose smooth ρ with dd^cρ≥h. The closed positive current dd^c(w+ρ)=H_w+(dd^cρ−h) then has uniformly bounded trace mass. The permitted local Lelong mass estimate and a finite cover give ν(w,x)≤L_h. Therefore, if for every δ>0 an actual δh-psh function v_δ≤u exists, Lelong comparison gives
  0≤ν(u,x)≤ν(v_δ,x)=δν(v_δ/δ,x)≤δL_h.
Letting δ↓0 proves ν(u,x)=0.

Mass conservation. Assume dd^c(h^k)=0 for 1≤k<n, and V=∫h^n. For every bounded genuine h-psh w, expansion and weighted Stokes give
  ∫(h+dd^c w)^n=V.
Indeed, for 1≤j≤n,
  ∫(dd^c w)^j∧h^(n−j)
  =∫w(dd^c w)^(j−1)∧dd^c(h^(n−j))=0;
for j=n use dd^c1=0. The signed mixed terms are defined by the supplied smooth-factor BT expansion; bounded approximation and weighted Stokes justify the computation for nonsmooth bounded w. The identical argument for δh gives total mass δ^n V.

For any genuine h-psh u, shift its supremum to zero and set u_j=max(u,−j), μ_j=(h+dd^c u_j)^n, μ=MA_h^ext(u). Finite-level locality identifies μ_j with μ on {u>−j}. Since μ_j(X)=V and these sets exhaust the non-pluripolar measure, μ(X)≤V. In particular the extended mass is finite on this background.

Let M=∫f dV>0. Any subsolution μ≥c f dV gives c≤V/M. Conversely the granted bounded-equation normalization characterization for f_k=min(f,k), together with bounded mass conservation, gives b_k∫f_k dV=V. Passing to the stipulated decreasing limit yields b_h(f)=V/M. For a threshold subsolution μ≥b_h(f)f dV, the right side has mass V while μ(X)≤V. Hence μ(X)=V and μ=b_h(f)f dV.

Actual canonical smaller-background competitor. Let μ(X)=V and fix 0<δ<1. Put v_j=P_(δh)(u_j). The constant −j is a competitor, so the assessed bounded-envelope theorem applies; −j≤v_j≤0. Its quasi-everywhere inequality v_j≤u_j is everywhere by the canonical mean-value argument. Let C_j={v_j=u_j}. Contact support, positivity after adding (1−δ)h, and the assessed h-contact comparison yield
  δ^n V=∫_{C_j}MA_(δh)(v_j)
  ≤∫_{C_j}MA_h(v_j)≤μ_j(C_j).
Both v_j and u_j are bounded h-psh, as required for that comparison.

Choose K>0 such that μ({u>−K})>(1−δ^n)V. For j>K, locality gives
  μ_j({u_j≤−K})=V−μ({u>−K})<δ^n V.
If sup v_j<−K, then C_j⊂{u_j≤−K}, contradicting the preceding inequality. Thus sup v_j≥−K. The envelopes decrease with their obstacles. Their decreasing limit v_δ is canonical δh-psh or identically −∞. To exclude the latter, take maximizers x_j and a convergent subsequence x_j→x. For each fixed l and all sufficiently large j, v_l(x_j)≥v_j(x_j)≥−K. Upper semicontinuity implies v_l(x)≥−K, hence v_δ(x)≥−K.

At every point,
  v_δ=lim_j v_j≤lim_j u_j=u.
This includes every pole: v_δ=−∞ wherever u=−∞. Thus v_δ is an actual canonical global competitor. Every other δh-psh competitor w≤u satisfies w≤v_j for every j and hence w≤v_δ. Since v_δ itself is a competitor, the raw supremum equals v_δ, already canonically upper semicontinuous. Consequently P_(δh)(u)=v_δ is genuine for every 0<δ<1. The uniform Lelong argument proves zero Lelong numbers. No dual attainment was used.

The non-Kähler Hopf instance. On C²\{0}, let s=|z|², Ω=dd^c s, h=s^(−1)Ω. The free properly discontinuous holomorphic action z↦2z multiplies s and Ω by four, so h descends smoothly and positively to the connected compact complex surface; a closed radial annulus is a compact fundamental region. The chain rule gives
  dd^c h=(−s^(−2)Ω+2s^(−3)ds∧d^c s)∧Ω=0,
because ds∧d^c s∧Ω=(s/2)Ω² in dimension two. However dh=−s^(−2)ds∧Ω is nonzero; at (r,0), its radial-first-coordinate and two-real-second-coordinate component is nonzero. Thus this specified h is not closed. With the stipulated normalization, the angularly integrated radial measure Ω² is 2s ds. On 1≤s≤4 the quotient volume is
  V=∫_1^4 2 ds/s=4 log 2.

For nonconstant smooth real q, choose sufficiently small nonzero ε so A=h+dd^c(εq)>0, and set u=εq−sup(εq), dV=h²/V, f=A²/dV, T=A/V. Mass conservation gives ∫A²=V, so M=V and b_h(f)=1. The normalized smooth u solves MA_h(u)=f dV. Moreover dd^c T=0 and ∫h∧T=V^(−1)∫h∧A=1 by dd^c h=0 and Stokes. T is smooth strictly positive, with root γ=A/V, and direct substitution gives D_p(T)=∫A²/V=1.

For every other normalized smooth positive Gauduchon test S=η^(n−1), arithmetic–geometric mean gives
  (A^n)^(1/n)(η^n)^((n−1)/n)≤A∧η^(n−1).
In an η-unitary frame, the right side is the arithmetic mean of the eigenvalues times η^n and the left side their geometric mean times η^n. Every strictly positive (n−1,n−1) test has a smooth positive root: in the normalized cofactor identification, a test matrix B>0 has root matrix (det B)^(1/(n−1))B^(−1), whose adjugate is B. Uniqueness makes this construction coordinate invariant. Here n=2. Therefore
  D_p(S)≤∫A∧S=∫h∧S+∫u dd^c S=1.
T is an actual maximizer over ALL normalized positive smooth tests. Granted attained uniqueness identifies Phi_f=u canonically.

notes.text:
Independent reconstruction B.

Write U=X\Z and A=h+dd^c Phi_f. The exact attained equation, finite mass and smoothness on U are granted background. Assume T=γ^(n−1), where γ is globally smooth semipositive with complex rank at least two everywhere, and Phi_f has zero Lelong numbers. On U, positivity of T implies positive definiteness of γ; A is smooth nonnegative there.

Proportionality from dual equality. The global measure β=A∧T is positive and well-defined because T is smooth semipositive and A is a positive order-zero current. Distributional Gauduchon Stokes gives β(X)=∫h∧T=1. On U, the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality established in n1 gives
  β≥(A^n)^(1/n)(γ^n)^((n−1)/n)=b^(1/n)p k_T dV.
The right side has mass b^(1/n)D_p(T)=1 and gives no mass to the proper analytic set Z. Equality of total masses forces equality on U and β(Z)=0. Equality in arithmetic–geometric mean for nonnegative eigenvalues says precisely that
  A=λγ on U,
where λ≥0 is smooth. This includes λ=0; no positivity of A or lower bound on f is assumed.

The rank condition. On real one-forms define L_γ(ξ)=ξ∧γ. It is injective when rank_C γ≥2. Diagonalize γ on its active real subspace W, of dimension 2r≥4. A complementary component of ξ cannot cancel an active component because the complementary degrees differ. On W, ξ∧γ=0 implies ξ∧γ^(r−1)=0 by wedging with γ^(r−2). The latter map from one-forms to (2r−1)-forms is an isomorphism in a symplectic basis. Hence ξ=0. With smooth background inner products,
  J=(L_γ*L_γ)^(−1)L_γ*
is a globally smooth left inverse, including at rank changes.

Since dA=dh, on U the proportionality gives
  dλ=a+λc,
  a=J(dh), c=−J(dγ),
where a and c are globally smooth one-forms. We prove extension of λ rather than assuming it.

Short paths and scalar extension. In a small real coordinate ball B, a and c are bounded. Two points of B/2\Z can be joined inside B by two line segments avoiding Z with total length at most four times the radius. Indeed, for a fixed endpoint, bad intermediate points belong to the cone of real rays through Z. A proper complex analytic set has real dimension at most 2n−2, so each such cone has dimension at most 2n−1 and Lebesgue measure zero. This can be checked on the countably many smooth strata of the analytic set and bounded intervals of the ray parameter. Thus an admissible intermediate point exists in any open ball. For endpoints distance d apart, an intermediate point in a radius-d ball gives length at most 3d within a slightly larger ball.

Fix x_0∈B/2\Z. Along these paths,
  |dλ/ds|≤K(1+λ).
Gronwall uniformly bounds λ by its finite value at x_0 and the bounded path length. The equation then uniformly bounds its gradient. The length-3d paths make λ locally Lipschitz on B/4\Z. It extends uniquely and nonnegatively across Z; the local extensions agree. Since Z has Lebesgue measure zero, the extended weak derivative still satisfies dλ=a+λc almost everywhere. The right side is continuous, so λ is C¹. Repeated differentiation bootstraps λ to C∞ globally.

Positive residual and analytic support. Set R=A−λγ. It has order zero and is supported on Z. The smooth form λγ has no mass on Z. Decomposing the matrix-valued measure A into restrictions to U and Z, its U-restriction is λγ and its Z-restriction is positive. Consequently R is precisely A restricted to Z and is positive. This proves the positivity of the residual rather than assuming positivity of a difference. Furthermore
  dR=dh−d(λγ)
is smooth and vanishes on dense U, hence vanishes everywhere.

At regular points of every irreducible divisorial component D of Z, the assessed support theorem for closed order-zero currents gives R=c_D[D], with c_D≥0 constant on the connected regular part. Let Q=Σc_D[D], a finite sum. Outside an analytic subset Y of complex dimension at most n−2, R=Q. Divisor integration currents give no mass to Y: their regular parts give no volume to smaller-dimensional analytic subsets, and their singular loci carry no integration-current mass. Thus R−Q=R restricted to Y is positive, closed and order zero. It is a normal current of bidimension (n−1,n−1) supported in dimension less than n−1. The supplied Demailly support theorem makes it zero. Therefore R=Σc_D[D]. At a generic regular point of D its Lelong number is c_D. Smooth forms have zero Lelong numbers, and the zero Lelong numbers of Phi_f make those of A and R zero. Every c_D is zero.

It follows that A=λγ is globally smooth and dd^c Phi_f=λγ−h is smooth. Taking the Euclidean trace locally and using distributional elliptic regularity makes Phi_f a smooth distributional potential. The canonical mean-value argument in n1 identifies this smooth representative with Phi_f at every point. This proves smoothness across all of Z. Independent reconstruction C.

Explicit canonical competitors on the specified arbitrary h. Assume ψ is genuine global quasi-psh, ψ≤0, dd^cψ≥−Ch, C>0, and canonically pointwise
  Phi_f≥−A(1−ψ)^α−B,
where A>0 and 0<α<1, with the stated −∞ interpretation at poles. Given 0<δ<1, choose t≥1 sufficiently large that
  CAαt^(α−1)≤δ,
and define
  v_δ=−A(t−ψ)^α−B,
with value −∞ at every pole of ψ. The function χ_t(s)=−A(t−s)^α−B is increasing and convex for s≤0, with 0<χ_t′≤Aαt^(α−1) and χ_t″≥0. Hence
  dd^cχ_t(ψ)≥−CAαt^(α−1)h≥−δh.
For singular ψ, this chain rule is justified by ψ_j=max(ψ,−j), local smooth psh regularizations after adding a fixed smooth local potential, the smooth chain rule, and bounded decreasing limits. Smoothness of h makes the error in the lower Hessian bound tend to zero. The positive second-derivative term is retained. Thus χ_t(ψ_j) are bounded δh-psh and decrease to χ_t(ψ). The limit is not identically −∞ because ψ is genuine and finite almost everywhere, and it is canonical, including its pole values.

Since t≥1,
  v_δ≤−A(1−ψ)^α−B≤Phi_f
at every point. This is an actual global competitor. The upper-regularized supremum of the nonempty competitor family is genuine δh-psh. To justify this canonically, the family is locally uniformly bounded above by the upper semicontinuous Phi_f and bounded below by v_δ. On sufficiently small coordinate balls, add quadratic potentials with constant Hessians dominating δh with arbitrarily small errors; the upper envelope then becomes psh. Let the errors tend to zero to obtain dd^c P≥−δh. The lower competitor excludes identically −∞. Upper regularization remains below Phi_f because Phi_f is upper semicontinuous; thus all required pole values are retained. Equivalently, the decreasing bounded envelopes P_(δh)(max(Phi_f,−j)) are bounded below by v_δ, and their limit is the same envelope by n1's maximality argument.

The all-δ competitors and n1's uniform Lelong bound prove ν(Phi_f,x)=0 everywhere. Together with exactly n2's globally smooth root and rank assumptions, this proves smooth extension across Z. Without those assumptions, this argument asserts neither boundedness nor continuity across Z.

Divisor logarithms. For an effective divisor D with defining section s of a line bundle L and smooth Hermitian metric H, set ψ=log|s|_H² minus its finite supremum. Poincaré–Lelong in the stipulated normalization gives
  dd^cψ=[D]−Θ_H.
Compactness gives Θ_H≤Ch for some C>0. Thus ψ is a permissible genuine global quasi-psh control function, canonically −∞ on D. This constructs ψ; it does not assert that an arbitrary Phi_f satisfies the required lower bound.

The projective example. On P^n, n≥2, let h=ω_FS, ∫h^n=1, dV=h^n, and
  ψ=log(Σ_(i=1)^n|z_i|²/Σ_(i=0)^n|z_i|²),
  u=1−(1−ψ)^α, 0<α<1,
  o=[1:0:…:0].
Local numerator potentials log Σ_(i=1)^n|z_i|² are psh with their canonical pole at o. Subtracting the local FS potential gives dd^cψ≥−h. Its sole pole is o; it is smooth elsewhere, ψ≤0, and ψ=0 along z_0=0.

For χ(s)=1−(1−s)^α,
  χ′(s)=α(1−s)^(α−1)≤α<1,
  χ″(s)=α(1−α)(1−s)^(α−2)>0.
The preceding composition argument gives genuine canonical h-psh u, smooth off o, u(o)=−∞, and sup u=0. In fact, globally as currents,
  h+dd^c u≥(1−α)h.
Off o this is immediate from
  h+dd^c u=(1−χ′)h+χ′(h+dd^cψ)+χ″dψ∧d^cψ;
truncation proves the global assertion. The quantitative bound is exact: A=1, B=−1, C=1. Actual smaller-background competitors are 1−(t−ψ)^α with t≥1 and αt^(α−1)≤δ. These also prove zero Lelong numbers. Full mass is established separately below.

Exact full mass ONE. In the affine chart z_0=1, write x=(z_1,…,z_n), t=|x|²>0, and
  L(t)=1+log((1+t)/t),
  a(t)=αL(t)^(α−1),
  H(t)=log(1+t)+1−L(t)^α,
  g(t)=tH′(t)=(t+a(t))/(1+t).
On this punctured chart A_u:=h+dd^c u=dd^c H(t). Direct differentiation gives
  a′(t)=α(1−α)L(t)^(α−2)/(t(1+t)),
  g′(t)=(1−a(t))/(1+t)²+a′(t)/(1+t)>0.
Relative to dd^c|x|², the n−1 tangential eigenvalues are g/t and the radial eigenvalue is g′. Therefore
  A_u^n=[(g/t)^(n−1)g′](dd^c|x|²)^n.
Our normalization gives (dd^c|x|²)^n=(n!/π^n)dLebesgue, whose angularly integrated radial measure is nt^(n−1)dt. Consequently
  ∫_{ε<t<R}A_u^n=g(R)^n−g(ε)^n.
As t↓0, a(t)→0 and g(t)→0. As t→∞, g(t)→1. Hence ∫_(C^n\{0})A_u^n=1. The hyperplane z_0=0 carries no mass because u and its Hessian are smooth there. The extended non-pluripolar measure equals A_u^n off o and assigns zero mass to its pole by its finite-level definition. Thus
  MA_h^ext(u)(P^n)=1.
This is an independent full-mass calculation, not an inference from zero Lelong numbers.

Density and lack of Lp improvement. Set f=A_u^n/h^n off o and, for definiteness, f(o)=0. Then MA_h^ext(u)=f dV, f is nonzero L1, and ∫f dV=1. Since the FS determinant in this chart is (1+t)^(−n−1),
  f(t)=(1+t)^(n+1)g(t)^(n−1)g′(t)/t^(n−1).
As t↓0,
  g(t)~αL(t)^(α−1),
  g′(t)~α(1−α)t^(−1)L(t)^(α−2),
and therefore
  f(t)~α^n(1−α)t^(−n)L(t)^(−[n(1−α)+1]).
Every asymptotic coefficient is positive. The L1 radial integral is comparable to t^(−1)(log(1/t))^(−[n(1−α)+1])dt, which is integrable. For any p>1, the Lp integral is bounded below by a positive constant times
  ∫_0 t^(n−1−np)(log(1/t))^(−p[n(1−α)+1])dt,
which diverges after t=e^(−s). Thus f belongs to no Lp with p>1.

Threshold identification. The Kähler h satisfies n1's specified-background condition, so b_h(f)=V/M=1. The normalized u is a threshold solution. Every threshold subsolution has full mass and this same measure by n1. The precisely assessed BEGZ Theorem 3.1 and Section 3.3 uniqueness apply to positive closed currents in [h], whose class volume is one, and to the constructed non-pluripolar measure of mass one. They make every such current equal to h+dd^c u. The differences of potentials have dd^c=0, are distributionally harmonic and hence smooth pluriharmonic, and are constant on connected compact P^n. Canonical equality and normalization give Phi_f=u everywhere, including o. No attainment assumption was used.

No smooth semipositive maximizer of the required kind. Suppose a normalized smooth semipositive Gauduchon T, positive outside a proper analytic set Z, attains D_p(T)=1. On P^n\(Z∪{o}) its positive root is smooth. The positive global measure A_u∧T has mass one by distributional Stokes; p k_T dV also has mass one and gives no mass to Z∪{o}. The AM–GM nonnegative-defect argument of n2 therefore forces equality on that open set. Since A_u is positive definite off o,
  T=c A_u^(n−1), c>0
there. Define on all P^n\{o}
  c=(A_u∧T)/A_u^n.
The denominator is smooth positive; c is smooth nonnegative. The tensor identity extends across Z\{o} by continuity, since its complement is dense. As A_u is closed, dd^c T=0 becomes
  dd^c c∧A_u^(n−1)=0
on the whole punctured manifold. This is an elliptic scalar harmonic equation for the smooth positive Kähler metric A_u, with local ellipticity sufficient.

Smoothness of T at o forces c→0 there. Indeed, the two radial eigenvalue types satisfy
  g(t)/t~α/(tL(t)^(1−α))→∞,
  g′(t)~α(1−α)/(tL(t)^(2−α))→∞.
Their minimum m(t) tends to infinity, so A_u≥m(t)dd^c|x|² and A_u^(n−1)≥m(t)^(n−1)(dd^c|x|²)^(n−1). The Euclidean trace of smooth T is bounded near o. Wedging T=cA_u^(n−1) with dd^c|x|² gives
  0≤c≤K/m(t)^(n−1)→0.
Here n−1>0. Define c(o)=0. The resulting continuous nonnegative function on compact P^n is positive somewhere, so its positive maximum occurs away from o. The strong maximum principle for the displayed elliptic equation on connected P^n\{o} makes c constant there, contradicting its zero limit. This excludes every smooth semipositive Gauduchon maximizer positive outside a proper analytic set, without any smooth-root assumption at o.

For a smooth positive Hermitian form ω, without a closedness assumption, bounded ω-psh functions have positive Monge–Ampère measures with plurifine maximum locality. If bounded ω-psh x≤y, then 1_{x=y}MA_ω(x)≤1_{x=y}MA_ω(y).

On a compact complex manifold with smooth positive Hermitian ω, a bounded quasicontinuous obstacle g whose quasi-everywhere envelope P_ω(g) is nonempty and finite has a bounded ω-psh upper-regularized envelope, lying below g quasi-everywhere, whose Monge–Ampère measure is concentrated on {P_ω(g)=g}.

Locally uniformly upper-bounded psh families have psh upper-regularized suprema. Decreasing psh sequences have psh limits, either locally integrable or identically −∞ on each connected component. Shrinking ball means recover canonical psh values.
Every connected compact complex manifold of dimension n≥2 admits a smooth positive Hermitian form γ satisfying dd^c(γ^(n−1))=0.
For a positive closed (1,1)-current B on B(x,R)⊂C^n, ν(B,x)≤C_n R^(−2n+2)∫_{B(x,R)}B∧ω_E^(n−1). Canonical quasi-psh v≤u implies ν(u,x)≤ν(v,x).
A proper analytic subset of a complex n-manifold admits a locally finite smooth complex stratification with strata of complex dimension at most n−1.

A positive closed (1,1)-current supported on a proper analytic subset is a locally finite sum ∑c_D[D] over its irreducible divisorial components, with constant c_D≥0. Support in codimension at least two forces the current to vanish.

With dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π), a nonzero holomorphic section s of a holomorphic line bundle with smooth Hermitian metric H satisfies dd^c log|s|_H²=[div(s)]−Θ_H, where Θ_H=−dd^c log|e|_H² in a local nonvanishing holomorphic frame e.

On a connected compact Kähler manifold (X,ω), genuine ω-psh functions with equal non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère measures, each of total mass ∫_Xω^n, differ by a constant; no finite-energy hypothesis is required.

On a connected manifold, a smooth real second-order elliptic operator with locally definite principal part and no zeroth-order term has the strong maximum property: a C² solution Lw=0 attaining its global maximum at an interior point is constant.
